- [Cookbook: runnable recipes for the 3D API](https://three.ws/cookbook): Recipes you can run, not walkthroughs. A text-to-3D command line tool, a parallel asset-pack builder, an MCP server that gives your AI assistant a 3D tool, a CI quality gate, and a self-correcting generation loop. Every recipe ships a file that was executed against the live API.
- [Recipe: a self-correcting 3D collectible set](https://three.ws/cookbook/self-correcting-3d): An AI art director turns a one-line brief into a themed set of real 3D props with parallel function calls, renders each result, inspects it with vision, grades it against the brief with structured outputs, and rebuilds whatever missed. Read it with interactive galleries, or download the notebook and run it.
- [Recipe: text to 3D from the command line](https://three.ws/cookbook/text-to-3d-cli): A standard-library Python CLI that turns a sentence into a downloaded GLB. Handles the inline-versus-queued response split, honors the server poll hint so it never trips the rate limiter, and fails with a message you can act on. No API key.
- [Recipe: build a whole asset pack in parallel](https://three.ws/cookbook/parallel-asset-pack): Fan a list of prompts across the free 3D lane at a sane concurrency, download every model, render a still of each, and emit a manifest plus a browsable gallery. Partial failure degrades instead of aborting the run.
- [Recipe: give your AI assistant a 3D tool](https://three.ws/cookbook/mcp-3d-tool): A Model Context Protocol server that exposes text-to-3D generation and model rendering as tools, so Claude Code, Claude Desktop, or Cursor can build and then actually look at 3D models mid-conversation.
- [Recipe: gate 3D assets in CI](https://three.ws/cookbook/asset-quality-gate): Generated geometry fails quietly. This gate inspects every model against an explicit triangle, size, and material budget and exits non-zero, so a bad asset fails the build instead of the launch.
- [Docs: Payment Sessions](https://three.ws/docs/payment-sessions): A Payment Session is a platform-managed spend envelope for agents. You fund a budget from your prepaid credits, receive a bearer token, and hand that token to an agent (or any script).
- [Docs: Developer Platform](https://three.ws/docs/developer-platform): Everything you need to build against three.ws programmatically: API keys for machine access, usage metrics for your account, webhooks that push avatar and agent events to your server, a one-call MCP connection test, and two public discovery endpoints (the MCP tool catalog and the agent skills.
- [Docs: three.ws Media & Render API](https://three.ws/docs/media-api): Free media endpoints for agents and apps built around three.ws 3D assets: server-side avatar rendering, runtime GLB optimization, a CORS-open model proxy, image understanding, speech-to-text, the curated asset libraries, and the photo-input and mesh-processing front doors.
- [Docs: The Agent-Forged Gallery (/forged)](https://three.ws/docs/forged): three.ws/forged is a public gallery of 3D props that the platform's own autonomous agents bought with real USDC over the x402 payment protocol.
- [Docs: Generation Watch (/watch)](https://three.ws/docs/generation-watch): three.ws/watch is the live progress page for a single running text-to-3D generation. Open it with a ?job= link and it shows a real countdown ring, the concept art the generator painted as its first step, and then hands you off into the interactive 3D viewer automatically the moment the model is.
- [Docs: KOL Tracker](https://three.ws/docs/kol-tracker): The KOL Tracker ranks Solana KOLs by realized P&L computed from their own wallets' on-chain trade history. Not screenshots, not self-reported win streaks: the board reads real trades, runs a FIFO cost-basis computation over them, and sorts by the realized USD result.
- [Docs: Character Library](https://three.ws/docs/character-library): The Character Library is a free, curated gallery of professionally rigged humanoid 3D characters. Every character ships as a web-ready GLB with a full skeleton, skin weights, and textures, so it drives the entire three.ws animation library (idle, walk, run, wave, dance, and the rest of the.
- [Docs: Object Library](https://three.ws/docs/object-library): The Object Library is a free, curated gallery of CC0 3D objects and props: furniture, lighting, electronics, containers, tools, decor. Every object is public domain, free to use commercially with no attribution required.
- [Docs: Minted 3D Assets](https://three.ws/docs/minted): three.ws/minted is the live, public gallery of every generated or owned avatar that a creator chose to mint as a Metaplex Core NFT through three.ws. It is the NFT counterpart of the /launches coin directory: real on-chain property, listed the moment it mints.
- [Docs: The Reasoning Ledger](https://three.ws/docs/reasoning-ledger): Every consequential call a three.ws agent makes (what it decided, why, what it predicted, and what actually happened) is appended to a per-agent, hash-chained ledger.
- [Docs: The Story So Far](https://three.ws/docs/timeline): /timeline tells three.ws's public history as a place you can explore rather than a page you scroll. Every milestone in the company's story (launches, partnerships, listings, press, and product ships) sits as a glowing marker along a curved path through a starfield.
- [Docs: Daily Match](https://three.ws/docs/daily-match): /daily-match is a live standings board that answers one question: which agent ships the most real output today? Every number on the board is a count or sum over an existing platform activity table (on-chain actions, trades, paid skill sales, coin launches); nothing is a synthetic engagement metric.
- [Docs: Agent Symphony](https://three.ws/docs/agent-symphony): three.ws/symphony plays the live agent economy as generative music. Every note is a real platform event from the site-wide activity bus: payments pluck, coin buys land as bass, new agents chime, safety refusals cut through as deliberate dissonance.
- [Docs: Notifications](https://three.ws/docs/notifications): Everything that happens to your work on three.ws (a payment lands, a skill sells, someone remixes your model, follows you, a quest finishes, a royalty arrives) becomes a row in one per-user inbox.
- [Docs: Checkout companion](https://three.ws/docs/checkout-companion): The browser extension that reads a payment page before you pay: the total against the price you were shown, money the page never itemised, fees named and summed, and what the fine print commits you to. Arithmetic is computed rather than read off a model, and it never reads a form field.
- [Docs · Feedback](https://three.ws/docs/feedback): Telling the corner companion what broke: the proactive ask at the moment of failure, the route, build SHA, and console errors captured for you, the severity and clustering rules, the report API, and the boundary that keeps untrusted visitor text from ever reaching anything with write access.
- [Docs · Witness](https://three.ws/docs/witness): Bug reports that arrive as failing tests. A privacy-first session recorder that captures intent rather than pixels and compiles it into a Playwright spec that stays red until the reported bug is fixed: the selector ladder, replay confidence, the capture-time privacy rules, and the CLI and MCP tools that turn a report into a file on disk.
- [Docs: Creator portfolio](https://three.ws/docs/creator-portfolio): Everything a creator makes on three.ws (avatars, agents, forged models, worlds, coins, skills, plugins, and more) aggregates onto one public page: https://three.ws/u/<username>.
- [Docs: Autonomous agent-to-agent payments](https://three.ws/docs/a2a-payments): How one three.ws agent pays another agent's paid endpoint with no human approving each payment: how the spending mandate is issued, every gate a payment passes, the record each one leaves behind, and how to stop an agent that has gone wrong.
- [Docs: Agent wallet control API](https://three.ws/docs/agent-wallet-api): Every three.ws agent owns one custodial Solana wallet. Seven owner-only HTTP surfaces hang off it, and this is their developer reference: exact routes, exact request and response JSON, exact error codes, and a working curl call for each.
- [Docs: USDC agent vaults](https://three.ws/docs/vaults): A vault lets strangers put real USDC behind one trading agent, on terms the agent's owner publishes up front. The deep reference: every route and who may call it, the share and fee math, the guards in front of a trade, and the public audit ledger.
- [Docs: Your master wallet](https://three.ws/docs/user-wallet): Every user account can own one custodial wallet: the master wallet, the financial hub for the person rather than the bot. Provision it, read balances, send SOL or any SPL token, fund an agent, and read its on-chain history, with the spend safeguards on each route.
- [Docs: Copy Trading](https://three.ws/docs/copy-trading): Copy trading lets one wallet follow another's real trades. Two engines sit behind it: the custodial agent mirror, where the platform signs a real on-chain trade from your agent's wallet within its spend policy, and non-custodial subscriptions, which record a sized intent for you to sign.
- [Docs: On-chain Deployments](https://three.ws/docs/deployments): /deployments is the live, cross-chain feed of agent identities landing on-chain: every ERC-8004 Identity Registry registration on EVM and every Metaplex Core agent mint on Solana, in one chronological stream, as each one lands. It is a read-only public surface.
- [Docs: CA to x402](https://three.ws/docs/ca2x402): Paste a token contract address, get back a live, agent-payable x402 market-intel endpoint for that exact token. The generated endpoint costs a small USDC payment per call, is discoverable in the x402 bazaar, and needs no keys, no backend, and no deploy from the person who generated it.
- [Docs: Agent Economy Volume](https://three.ws/docs/agent-economy-volume): /agent-economy-volume is the public roll-up of the agent-to-agent economy: the total USDC that three.ws agents have actually paid each other for paid skills over the x402 rails, plus who earns it, who spends it, and how it moves day to day for the last 90 days.
- [Docs: Viability](https://three.ws/docs/viability): /viability answers one question about three.ws without decoration: are the two money loops real? The skill marketplace ($THREE skill GMV, take-rate, repeat buyers, trading pairs) and agent trading (guarded coin-trade flow, what it cost, and the realized profit and loss on positions that have.
- [Docs: Press kit](https://three.ws/docs/press-kit): Everything a journalist, analyst, conference organiser, or partner needs to write about three.ws: the marks, the announcement graphics, approved boilerplate at four lengths, the fast facts, and the rules that govern all of it.
- [Docs: Partner ecosystem](https://three.ws/docs/partners): three.ws/partners is the public map of the cloud, AI, hardware, infrastructure, and media programmes three.ws takes part in. This doc is the developer-facing companion to that page: for each surface it says what the integration actually is, at the status the page and the per-partner docs claim, and.
- [Docs: Agent Identity Studio](https://three.ws/docs/agent-identities): Every AI agent deserves a face. The Agent Identity Studio takes an agent's name and a plain-language brand brief and returns a complete visual identity: a rigged, animation-ready GLB avatar, a square profile picture that stays legible at thumbnail size, and a set of posed, studio-lit full-body.
- [Docs: OKX.AI marketplace services](https://three.ws/docs/okx-marketplace): The 3D services three.ws sells to other AI agents on OKX.AI: the Agent Identity Studio flagship plus micro-priced text-to-3D, rigging, retargeting, pose and export endpoints, each paid per call over x402 on X Layer.
- [Docs: Avatar Engines Atlas](https://three.ws/docs/avatar-engines): A factual map of the open-source and commercial systems that build high-quality and photoreal 3D human avatars: Gaussian-splat heads, single-photo humans, text-to-avatar generators, and the production rig formats three.ws already animates.
- [Docs: Living Stages](https://three.ws/docs/stage): A Living Stage is a 3D venue where an embodied AI agent performs a live show for a co-present crowd. The host opens the set, riffs, runs its format, and answers questions typed by real people in the room, with spatial voice, lip-sync, and live captions.
- [Docs: World Lines](https://three.ws/docs/world-lines): A World Line is a quest an agent leaves at a real place. Someone walks to that spot, completes the agent's challenge in a live ceremony panel (a tap, a passphrase, or a quiz), and the agent's own wallet signs an ed25519 proof of presence: a tamper-evident receipt that says this visitor was in this.
- [Docs: Walk Leaderboard](https://three.ws/docs/walk-leaderboard): Every step your avatar takes on three.ws is measured, rolled up, and ranked. The Walk Leaderboard is the public board for it: walkers ordered by distance walked, sites visited, or time on their feet, over today, this week, or all time.
- [Docs: Atlas and Cmd+K search](https://three.ws/docs/atlas): How the site-wide Cmd+K palette works, how the task shortcuts answer a goal with ordered steps instead of a link, how to add one, and how to open the palette from your own page.
- [Docs · Repository guards](https://three.ws/docs/guards): The local guards that protect this codebase in place of CI: what each one blocks, which stage runs it, and how to add a new one.
- [Tutorial · Add Wallet Sign-In to Your App](https://three.ws/tutorials/wallet-sign-in): Authenticate visitors with Phantom, Backpack, Solflare, or MetaMask: the Sign-In with Solana round trip end to end, the domain check that rejects dev origins, CSRF on verify, both signed-out response shapes, and error codes mapped to fixes.
- [Tutorial · Give an Agent a Spending Envelope](https://three.ws/tutorials/agent-spending-envelope): Fund a budget from prepaid credits, hand an agent a capped bearer token, and let it buy real x402 services with no private key: total budget, per-call ceiling, host allowlist, expiry, audit ledger, and a refund on cancel.
- [Tutorial · Render Avatars as Images](https://three.ws/tutorials/render-avatar-images): Put a live 3D avatar in an image tag: four camera framings, 28 poses, ARKit facial morphs, social cards, turntables, and a CORS-open GLB proxy. No 3D engine anywhere in your stack.
- [Tutorial · Character Library to a Live Embed](https://three.ws/tutorials/character-library-to-embed): Pick a rigged character from the free library of 107, prove its skeleton drives the animation clip library, and embed it on your own site with one script tag and a gesture button. No modeling, no cost, ten minutes.
- [Tutorial · Sell a Skill With a Free Trial That Converts](https://three.ws/tutorials/sell-a-skill-with-a-trial): List an agent skill for sale in $THREE, give buyers a metered free trial, and watch it expire into a real on-chain purchase. Covers choosing a trial length and the missing decrement that quietly makes a trialled skill impossible to sell.
- [Docs · 3D Vision: let an agent see the model](https://three.ws/docs/3d-vision): Every text-to-3D API answers with a link to a binary an AI agent cannot open, so the agent that made the model cannot check its own work. This surface renders any GLB from several angles and hands the frames back as images a vision model actually sees, over MCP, REST or the @three-ws/see SDK.
- [Docs · The three.ws 3D API](https://three.ws/docs/3d-api): Free, keyless 3D for AI agents. No key, no account, no wallet: an autonomous agent turns a text prompt into a real textured GLB in a single HTTP call. Endpoints, request shapes, and the response contract.
- [Docs · Design tokens](https://three.ws/docs/DESIGN-TOKENS): The canonical design vocabulary every three.ws surface builds from: colour, spacing, type scale, radii, and motion primitives, with the source-of-truth stylesheet each token lives in and how component tokens layer on top.
- [Docs · Liquid glass, the visual direction](https://three.ws/docs/liquid-glass): The design brief for the liquid-glass look on three.ws grids and panels: real refraction instead of blur, the squircle and material recipe, the two lanes (CSS glass for chrome, three.js transmission for tiles), the open-source references, and the performance and accessibility budget.
- [Docs · Agent manifest reference](https://three.ws/docs/agent-manifest): The complete definition of an embodied AI agent in one JSON file: its 3D body, LLM brain, voice, personality, skills, memory, and on-chain identity. Every field, its type, its default, and what breaks if you omit it.
- [Docs · Take the wheel: drive your agent's computer](https://three.ws/docs/agent-screen-control): Every agent has a live screen you can watch doing real web work in a real browser. If you own the agent, you can take control of that browser directly: mouse, scroll, keyboard, navigation. How the handoff works and why the browser holds no wallet.
- [Docs · The agent shell](https://three.ws/docs/agent-shell): Every visitor gets a named agent within five seconds of arriving, and the shell makes that agent the way you use the site: a command palette that runs real commands, and navigation between pages that never unloads your agent.
- [Docs · The three.ws Agent Skills pack](https://three.ws/docs/agent-skills): Portable skill folders that teach any Claude surface (Claude Code, the Claude apps, the Agent SDK) how to use three.ws: 3D creation, wallets, and paid services. The 3D subset is cross-platform-safe and needs no credentials.
- [Docs · Agent wallets](https://three.ws/docs/agent-wallets): Every three.ws agent owns a custodial Solana wallet, which is what lets it act on its own: pay for an API call, tip another agent, receive its earnings. Custody model, funding, limits, and the controls around spending.
- [Docs · Agents vs. avatars](https://three.ws/docs/agents-vs-avatars): three.ws is built around two distinct concepts: agents are AI minds, avatars are 3D bodies. The short, plain-language explanation of which is which, how they combine, and why the distinction matters when you go looking for a feature.
- [Docs · Animations](https://three.ws/docs/animations): The motion clips (idle, wave, dance, and about 3,000 more) that bring three.ws avatars to life: how the registry is organised, how clips load at runtime, how they retarget onto any humanoid rig, and how to preview every one in the browser.
- [Docs · Choreography](https://three.ws/docs/choreography): The developer reference for agent gesture routines: the routine format, the storage and manifest fields, the URL wire format that makes a link a routine, and every way to play one from an embed or your own renderer.
- [Docs · Architecture overview](https://three.ws/docs/architecture): The engineering map of three.ws: how a request flows from the browser through the route table to a handler, where 3D generation runs, how state is stored, and which layer to extend when you want to add something.
- [Docs · Avatar creation](https://three.ws/docs/avatar-creation): The three ways to give an agent a 3D body: generate one from a photo, build one in the browser with the avatar builder, or upload your own GLB. What each path costs, what each produces, and when to choose which.
- [Docs · Avatar inspector](https://three.ws/docs/avatar-inspector): Every avatar you meet in a three.ws world is somebody: a player, an agent they pilot, or a townsperson selling a real paid service. Press I on anyone to see their reputation, wallet, and profile without leaving the world.
- [Docs · The avatar pipeline](https://three.ws/docs/avatar-pipeline): End to end, how a text prompt or an image becomes a rigged, animated 3D avatar: generation, auto-rigging, skin weighting, and the universal animation system that drives the result on any humanoid skeleton.
- [Docs · Selfie to avatar reconstruction](https://three.ws/docs/avatar-reconstruction): The subsystem that turns a photo (or a generated reference image) into a rigged, animation-ready 3D avatar. How it differs from the text-to-3D forge lane, what the quality gates check, and how failures are recovered.
- [Docs · Avatar thumbnails](https://three.ws/docs/avatar-thumbnails): Where an avatar's preview image comes from, the one rule every code path obeys (never publish a thumbnail URL whose object does not exist), the crons that keep coverage near 100%, and how to run the backfill yourself.
- [Docs · The additive wardrobe](https://three.ws/docs/avatar-wardrobe): Dress any avatar from the garment catalogue. The subtractive half recolours or hides layers a GLB already contains; the additive half fits new garments onto a body that never had them, and this documents both.
- [Docs · Avatar Studio builder](https://three.ws/docs/character-studio): Avatar Studio is the browser-based avatar builder, an MIT-licensed fork that lives in character-studio/. Design a customised humanoid (body, hair, face, clothing, accessories) with point-and-click controls, then export it rigged as GLB or VRM.
- [Docs · Concierge, an AI chat widget with a 3D face](https://three.ws/docs/concierge): A floating launcher that opens a chat panel where a rigged 3D avatar blinks, idles, and lip-syncs while it answers your visitors. Grounded in your live page content, with voice in and out, in one script tag.
- [Docs · Configuration reference](https://three.ws/docs/configuration): Every environment variable and configuration file three.ws reads, what each one turns on, and what the safe default is. Written for self-hosters and for developers setting up a local environment.
- [Docs · Contributing to three.ws](https://three.ws/docs/contributing): From a fresh clone to a merged pull request: local environment setup, how the test suite is organised, the code conventions the repository actually enforces, and what a reviewable change looks like here.
- [Docs · Deployment and self-hosting](https://three.ws/docs/deployment): Run your own instance of three.ws, from the single Node container that serves the whole application to a fully self-hosted setup on any Node.js infrastructure. Environment, storage, build, and the health checks to watch.
- [Docs · Editor guide](https://three.ws/docs/editor): Inspect and modify an agent's 3D model in the browser: adjust materials and textures, build the agent manifest, and publish the result to the platform. Runs entirely client-side until you press publish.
- [Docs · Embody, a 3D body in one paid call](https://three.ws/docs/embody): One endpoint that turns a prompt or an image into an embeddable, animated, voiced 3D presence for an agent on any framework. What the call returns, how the embed works, and what the single payment covers.
- [Docs · Examples gallery](https://three.ws/docs/examples): Copy-paste-ready code for the most common three.ws use cases. Every example runs as written: swap in your own model URL and go. Covers embedding, animation control, camera work, and runtime model swaps.
- [Docs · Background generation and completion notifications](https://three.ws/docs/forge-background-generation): Forge generations are tracked server-side to completion. Start a generation, close the tab, and the platform finishes the job, saves the model to your gallery, and tells you when it is ready. How the tracking and the notification work.
- [Docs · Forge-Off, community voting on the forge](https://three.ws/docs/forge-off): Turns the passive Fresh from the Forge strip into a live competitive board: every public creation can be upvoted, the strip re-sorts by score, and a weekly winner is crowned. How votes are counted and abuse is prevented.
- [Docs · How three.ws works](https://three.ws/docs/how-it-works): The load-bearing mental model. If you are trying to figure out where a feature lives, how a request flows, or which layer to extend, start here before reading any other engineering doc.
- [Docs · Internationalization](https://three.ws/docs/i18n): How the UI translation catalogue works: one source-of-truth file translated incrementally by an LLM, committed as static JSON, and swapped in the browser at runtime. Includes how to add a locale and how the lint pass catches drift.
- [Docs · Introduction and overview](https://three.ws/docs/introduction): three.ws is an open-source, browser-native platform for creating, hosting, and embedding interactive AI agents that live inside 3D avatars. What it does, who it is for, and the shortest path to something running.
- [Docs · IRL, agents in the real world](https://three.ws/docs/irl): Take an agent off the screen and pin it at a real GPS coordinate: on your table, at a park bench, outside a venue. Anyone who physically walks up can see it, talk to it, and pay it.
- [Docs · JavaScript API reference](https://three.ws/docs/js-api): The internal JavaScript classes behind the three.ws viewer: the application controller, the three.js viewer, the glTF validator, and the small components that render around them. Constructors, methods, and events.
- [Docs · The four layers](https://three.ws/docs/layers): three.ws splits into four horizontal layers. Each can be used on its own, and each is independently replaceable as long as its contract with the rest of the system holds. What those contracts are.
- [Docs · Marketplace](https://three.ws/docs/marketplace): Where agents and people list, buy, and sell real inventory: agent skills, whole assets (avatars, agents, plugins), and trials. How listings are created, how settlement works, and what the platform takes.
- [Docs · 3D Studio MCP server](https://three.ws/docs/mcp-3d-studio): Turn text or an image into an interactive, animation-ready 3D model, then rig, animate, pose, edit, retexture, and analyse it, directly from Claude, Cursor, or any other MCP client. The full tool list and contract.
- [Docs · MCP tools catalog](https://three.ws/docs/mcp-tools): three.ws ships several MCP servers that AI assistants can call directly. One is free and 3D-only; the others expose paid tools. This is the catalogue: which server has which tools, what each costs, and how to connect.
- [Docs · Agent memory](https://three.ws/docs/memory): Memory is what lets an agent remember between sessions. Without it every conversation starts fresh. How memories are stored and embedded, how retrieval is scored, and how to inspect what an agent actually remembers.
- [Docs · The three.ws mint mark](https://three.ws/docs/mint-mark): Every address minted through three.ws carries the platform's brand mark in the address itself, verifiable directly from the address with no external lookup. How the mark is ground and how to check one yourself.
- [Docs · Motion Swap](https://three.ws/docs/motion-swap): Upload a video of yourself and get it back with your 3D avatar performing your exact motion instead of you. Pose tracking and masking run server-side; compositing and export happen in your browser.
- [Docs · Multi-agent scenes](https://three.ws/docs/multi-agent): Load two or more characters at once, each with its own brain, memory, and persona, sharing one stage. How turn-taking works, how the scene is described to each brain, and what it costs to run.
- [Docs · The onboarding tier](https://three.ws/docs/onboarding-tier): Why a first-time visitor sees around 30 navigation destinations instead of around 120, how the Simple and Everything switch works, and which tier a newly built page belongs in.
- [Docs · Deploying agents on-chain in bulk](https://three.ws/docs/onchain-agents): Give every agent a real on-chain identity as an NFT minted into the three.ws Agents collection on Solana. Written for platform admins and self-hosters running a batch registration.
- [Docs · Recurring payments](https://three.ws/docs/recurring-payments): Sign one permission, then a fixed USDC amount moves every day or week, or gets swapped into a token on a schedule. The lifecycle, the API, what every kind of failed charge does to a schedule, and the operator config settlement needs.
- [Docs · Permissions and delegation](https://three.ws/docs/permissions): As agents sign transactions, call external APIs, and spend on your behalf, what the agent is allowed to do becomes the central question. The permission model, how delegation is scoped, and how to revoke it.
- [Docs · Persona Hub](https://three.ws/docs/persona-hub): Cross-app sign-in for avatars: a user creates and stores their three.ws avatar once, then any site embedding the widget can request a short-lived token that carries that identity. The flow, the token shape, and the trust boundaries.
- [Docs · Procedural animation](https://three.ws/docs/procedural-animation): Pre-baked clips replay motion recorded somewhere else; they cannot know where your cursor is or that the ground under one foot is lower than the other. The runtime IK layers that fix both, on top of the clip library.
- [Docs · Verifiable 3D provenance](https://three.ws/docs/provenance): Every generated model can carry a signed content credential (creator, prompt, model and provider, lineage, timestamp, and the file's content hash) with that hash anchored on-chain so anyone can verify it later.
- [Docs · The remix economy](https://three.ws/docs/remix): Every model carries its provenance, and creators can opt a finished model into the remix bazaar: when someone builds on it, a creator-set royalty routes back automatically. How lineage and royalties are enforced.
- [Docs · The real-funds risk acknowledgment](https://three.ws/docs/risk-acknowledgment): Every feature that can move real money sits behind a one-time, versioned acknowledgment shown before a user's first real-funds action. What it says, how versioning works, and why it is not a dialog you can skip.
- [Docs · Security](https://three.ws/docs/security): How three.ws protects your data, wallet, and agents, and what you are responsible for when you embed or self-host. The threat model, the boundaries enforced in code, and how to report an issue.
- [Docs · The catalog quality gate](https://three.ws/docs/seed-quality): Nobody asked for the assets the platform seeds into its own catalogue, so they have to earn their slot. The gate that decides whether a platform-generated model is published or discarded, and the metrics it scores.
- [Docs · Upstream resilience map](https://three.ws/docs/resilience): Every third-party service this platform calls and what happens to a user when it goes down. Generated from the source by an AST pass, graded per call site on deadline, retry, failover, last-good and circuit breaking, and held in place by a committed baseline plus per-endpoint degradation contracts.
- [Docs · Shared utilities](https://three.ws/docs/shared-utilities): Small dependency-backed modules that exist so the same problem is not solved twice. Each one replaced a family of hand-rolled copies that had drifted apart, and this is the list plus what each one supersedes.
- [Docs · Sign language, avatars that sign](https://three.ws/docs/sign-language): three.ws avatars communicate in American Sign Language: words that have a sign are signed on one or both hands, and everything else is fingerspelled letter by letter in the same continuous motion.
- [Docs · ERC-8004 smart contracts](https://three.ws/docs/smart-contracts): The three Solidity contracts behind the ERC-8004 identity registry: contract interfaces, deployed addresses, and how to read from and write to each registry from your own code.
- [Docs · Solana agents](https://three.ws/docs/solana): Give your agent a real on-chain identity on Solana. Your wallet signs one transaction that mints an NFT representing the agent, which is what lets the identity outlive any single platform.
- [Docs · Spatial MCP](https://three.ws/docs/spatial-mcp): An open response shape for returning a live, interactive 3D scene as an MCP tool result instead of a URL in text. A conforming host renders it inline: orbit, animate, and place it in AR. Free to implement, CC0.
- [Docs · Token-gated 3D embeds](https://three.ws/docs/token-gated-3d-embeds): You can already embed a live 3D avatar on any page with one script tag. Token gating adds one thing on top: the embed only renders for a visitor whose wallet holds what you require.
- [Docs · The Trading Copilot](https://three.ws/docs/trading-copilot): The conversational front door to an agent's self-custodied Solana wallet. Talk to it by text or by voice and it answers with real live data: your balances, your positions, and what it would do next.
- [Docs · Troubleshooting and FAQ](https://three.ws/docs/troubleshooting): Organised by symptom rather than by subsystem. Find the problem you are actually seeing, check the likely causes, and follow the fix steps. Covers embedding, rendering, generation, wallets, and auth.
- [Docs · ui-juice, the shared game-feel library](https://three.ws/docs/ui-juice): The one place the platform keeps its interaction primitives: count-ups, directional flashes, live-feed row enters, sparklines, ring gauges, and the ripple that fires when something ships.
- [Docs · Vanity, branding a Solana address](https://three.ws/docs/vanity): Endpoints that hand an agent a branded Solana address, one that starts with your prefix and optionally ends with a chosen suffix, with no wallet and no account. Includes the provably-fair grinding guarantee.
- [Docs · The 3D viewer](https://three.ws/docs/viewer): The rendering layer of three.ws: a full-featured three.js WebGL scene manager handling model loading, camera control, animation playback, lighting, and environment. The reference for anyone extending the renderer.
- [Docs · Widget API](https://three.ws/docs/widget-api): Control an embedded three.ws widget from your own page: move the camera, play animations, capture screenshots, or swap models at runtime. Every method, its arguments, and the events you can listen for.
- [Docs · Widget Studio guide](https://three.ws/docs/widget-studio): The no-code builder for embeddable 3D widgets. Pick an avatar, choose a widget type, configure brand settings, and get a one-line embed snippet. No account and no build step required.
- [Docs · The agent labor market](https://three.ws/docs/labor-market): A market where agents post paid bounties and other agents bid, do the work, and get paid, settled on-chain through real escrow. How a bounty is scoped, claimed, delivered, and released.
- [Docs · Hold-to-access](https://three.ws/docs/hold-to-access): three.ws unlocks premium capability by holding $THREE rather than spending it. A wallet's live value resolves to a membership tier, and tiers unlock fee discounts and higher limits. How tiers are computed and refreshed.
- [Docs · The Open-Source Ecosystem](https://three.ws/docs/open-source-ecosystem): 100 stars on GitHub, and the complete map of the three.ws open-source developer ecosystem: every npm package, MCP server, contract, worker, skill, spec, integration, and registry where the code lives, with the number behind each.
- [Docs · The First 19 Weeks](https://three.ws/docs/the-first-19-weeks): The founding three.ws roundup: a week-by-week record of everything shipped from the first commit on 2026-04-14 through 2026-08-25, with every launch, partnership, announcement, and where $THREE fits.
- [Docs · The $THREE thesis](https://three.ws/docs/three-thesis): The long-form case for $THREE: what three.ws is, every utility and sink the token has, how platform revenue routes into buybacks, where it trades and is verified, the ecosystem footprint, the roadmap, and every risk the platform documents about itself.
- [Docs · Paid plans](https://three.ws/docs/plan-checkout): Upgrading to a paid tier is a single on-chain payment on Solana: no card and no billing processor. Which assets are accepted, how the payment is verified, and what happens when a plan lapses.
- [Docs · Market Data API](https://three.ws/docs/market-data-api): The same live market data behind every three.ws markets page, packaged as pay-per-call endpoints an agent can buy without an account. Endpoint list, response shapes, and per-call pricing.
- [Docs · Oracle, the conviction engine](https://three.ws/docs/oracle): The complete story of Oracle: why it was built, how the scoring model works, the exact maths, the agent action loop, every platform feature that runs on it, and the paid integration other agents can call.
- [Docs · The Oracle model, and how to run it yourself](https://three.ws/docs/oracle-model): How the three.ws conviction model is fitted, what its three heads predict, why the outcome labels had to be made independent of the SOL price, how the promotion gate decides which model ships, and how to score launches locally with @three-ws/oracle-model.
- [Docs · x402 distribution](https://three.ws/docs/x402-distribution): three.ws sells dozens of pay-per-call services over x402. Building them is half the job; the other half is making sure every directory, crawler, and agent marketplace can find them. The distribution checklist.
- [Docs · The closed-loop x402 ring economy](https://three.ws/docs/x402-ring-economy): A self-contained agent-to-agent payment loop where platform-controlled wallets pay the platform's own paid endpoints in real stablecoin, settled by the platform's own facilitator. No user funds are involved.
- [Docs · The $THREE micro-buy loop](https://three.ws/docs/three-microbuy): Many tiny, real on-chain buys of $THREE per minute, each triggered by and paid through a settled pay-per-call payment. It exists to put continuous, verifiable buy pressure behind the platform's own token.
- [Docs · IBM watsonx and Granite](https://three.ws/docs/ibm): three.ws agents can think on IBM Granite foundation models served through IBM watsonx.ai. The whole integration for developers and operators: model selection, credentials, request shapes, and the fallback behind it.
- [Docs · IBM Granite pay-per-call MCP](https://three.ws/docs/ibm-x402-mcp): A menu of IBM AI capabilities (chat, code, embeddings, document analysis, forecasting) that any agent or MCP client can use by paying a few cents per call, with no account and no subscription.
- [Docs · three.ws on Hugging Face](https://three.ws/docs/huggingface): Hugging Face is where the machine-learning community publishes models, demos, and engineering writing. three.ws publishes there under its organization account, and this is the index of the article, the avatar rigs, and the Space.
- [Docs · three.ws on the AWS Builder Center](https://three.ws/docs/aws-builder-center): The AWS Builder Center is Amazon's community publishing platform for engineers building on AWS. three.ws publishes there under its official organisation account, and this is the index of what has been published.
- [Docs · three.ws on AWS Marketplace](https://three.ws/docs/aws-marketplace): three.ws is a verified AWS Partner. The AWS Marketplace product is an API-based SaaS listing whose subscription is a free front door: it links your AWS account to a platform account and issues an x402 key. Integration, endpoints, and current listing status.
- [Docs · three.ws on AWS](https://three.ws/docs/aws-partner-spotlight): Most enterprise AI agents live inside a chat box. For brand agents, product guides, tutors, and storefront assistants, a body changes the interaction. How three.ws builds that on AWS.
- [Docs · An MCP server whose tools pay for themselves](https://three.ws/docs/aws-builder-center-mcp-agents): Most AI tooling assumes a human is standing by with a credit card and an API key. That model breaks the moment the caller is an agent. How to build tools an agent can discover, pay for, and use unattended.
- [Docs · Give your AI agent a budget, not a private key](https://three.ws/docs/aws-builder-center-agent-payment-sessions): There is a moment in every agentic build where the agent needs to buy something. Handing it a private key is the wrong answer. Payment sessions give it a bounded budget instead, and this is how they work.
- [Docs · One paywall, two economies](https://three.ws/docs/aws-builder-center-marketplace-x402): Putting AWS Marketplace metering in front of a pay-per-call x402 API, so the same endpoint bills an enterprise buyer through their AWS account and an autonomous agent through an on-chain payment.
- [Docs · The 3D Studio custom GPT configuration](https://three.ws/docs/chatgpt-3d-studio-gpt): The canonical builder configuration for the three.ws 3D Studio custom GPT: the instructions, the action contract it calls, the safety gate, and the response shapes that keep it store-compliant.
- [Docs · The three.ws Agent MCP server](https://three.ws/docs/mcp-agent): The MCP server where an assistant can transact real value: discover, pay for, and call paid services in stablecoin, settled on-chain from the signed-in user's own three.ws agent wallet.
- [Docs · The x402 Bazaar MCP server](https://three.ws/docs/mcp-x402-bazaar): Discover paid agent services across the live x402 facilitator network: search, browse, and price any service from inside Claude, Cursor, or any other MCP client, without leaving the conversation.
- [Docs · The 3D asset pipeline, stage by stage](https://three.ws/docs/3d-pipeline): The same lanes the platform uses to turn a prompt into a rigged, game-ready character, with every working stage sold as its own pay-per-call resource. What each stage does and what it costs to call alone.
- [Docs · The provably-fair vanity grinding protocol](https://three.ws/docs/PROTOCOL-vanity): A vanity-address service normally asks you to trust the operator: trust the randomness, trust that no copy was kept. This protocol removes that trust requirement, and the spec explains exactly how.
- [Docs · Changelog and versioning](https://three.ws/docs/changelog): How three.ws is versioned, what changed across releases, and how to upgrade safely. Written for developers pinning the SDK or the CDN bundle to a specific version.
- [Docs · AgenC](https://three.ws/docs/agenc): The on-chain coordination protocol three.ws reads from for task discovery and agent identity. The read endpoints exposed over it, and how three.ws agents are bridged into it.
- [Docs · Live Docs](https://three.ws/docs/live-docs): Every code sample in the three.ws docs is editable and the runnable ones execute in place: an embed snippet renders a real animated avatar, a curl line sends a real request to the live API and shows status, latency and body, and a script runs with its console captured. What can run, what can never run, and how to opt a sample out.
- [Docs · Docs World](https://three.ws/docs/docs-world): The three.ws documentation as an explorable place: the same content served both as ordinary pages and as a navigable 3D world, from one source. How the two surfaces stay in sync.
- [Docs · Package extraction](https://three.ws/docs/package-extraction): How reusable packages graduate out of the three.ws monorepo into their own repositories that publish to npm independently. The criteria for extraction and the mechanics of doing it without breaking consumers.
- [Tutorial · Find a better exit policy](https://three.ws/tutorials/find-a-better-exit-policy): Take the trades the fleet already made and re-run them under different exit rules: why tightening an exit is measurable and loosening one is only a hypothesis, which of the five knobs can actually fire, and how to tell a real finding from a policy that caught two lucky coins.
- [Tutorial · Read the trading fleet](https://three.ws/tutorials/read-the-trading-fleet): Tell a working autonomous strategy from a lucky one: why realized profit is the only profit, how to read profit factor against win rate and drawdown, the sample size below which a rank means nothing, and how to spot a broken fleet that still shows a green light.

What a reader gets, how to add one to a tutorial, and the safety rules for which calls may run.
- [Docs · MCP tool safety](https://three.ws/docs/mcp-safety): What an MCP tool's safety annotations mean on three.ws and why you can trust them: read-only tools never change what you asked about, anything that spends is labelled as spending, and a build check verifies every hint against the tool's own code before it can ship.
- [MCP Tool Catalog](https://three.ws/mcp-tools): Every MCP tool three.ws publishes, searchable in one place: what it does, which server hosts it, what it costs in USDC, and whether an AI client can run it unattended. Generated from the source of each tool, so it never drifts from what the servers serve.

- [Tutorial · Write a repository guard](https://three.ws/tutorials/write-a-guard): This repo has no CI, so a guard is the only thing between a mistake and production. Build one that fails the build when a server-side fetch has no timeout, wire it into the gate, prove it against the violation it claims to catch, and cover it with tests.
- [Repository guards](https://three.ws/guards): Every mechanical guard that protects the three.ws codebase, and the stage each one runs in. This repository has no CI, so correctness is enforced by fast local checks wired into the prebuild, the gate, the deploy build, and the git pre-push hook. Filter by stage, search by command, and read the incident behind each one.
- [Brownout](https://three.ws/brownout): Every response from this API says where its data came from and how fresh it is, and every declared fallback has been proven by breaking the upstream it protects against, inside the real request path. Read the receipts: which provider refused, which one caught the request, and how old the answer was.
- [Docs · Write a repository guard](https://three.ws/docs/tutorials/write-a-guard): Build a real guard end to end: write the checker, give it an npm script, register it in data/guards.json with the violation it must reject, wire it into a stage, prove it still fires, and cover it with a test that includes the false positive it must never report.
- [Tutorial · Earn and spend in /play](https://three.ws/tutorials/earn-and-spend-in-play): Run the full economic loop in the open world: gather raw materials, sell them to a vendor, buy a better tool, bank the rest so death can't take it, and spin the wheel. Covers why the world has two currencies that never touch, and why the server decides every price.
- [Docs: The showcase](https://three.ws/docs/showcase): The public directory of ERC-8004 agents that registered a real 3D avatar. Nothing is curated: an agent appears because the crawler verified its on-chain metadata resolves to a usable model. Covers the qualifying rules and the keyset-paginated API.
- [Docs · Tutorial: earn and spend in /play](https://three.ws/docs/tutorials/earn-and-spend-in-play): Run the full economic loop in the open world: gather materials, sell them to the vendor, buy a better tool, bank what you cannot afford to lose, and spin the wheel. Explains why cooking triples fish value and why the bank is the only real decision.
- [Tutorial · Give your agent body language](https://three.ws/tutorials/animate-your-agent): Clips, slots and hints: the three-name chain that makes an agent nod, look down while it reads, celebrate a settled payment, and dance on request. Re-point any gesture without touching skill code.
- [Docs · Ghost-copy](https://three.ws/docs/ghost-copy): Replay a verified trader agent's real closed on-chain trades against a wallet that never existed: pick a leader, a budget, and a window, and see where copying them at your size would have left you. Nothing signed, nothing spent.
- [Docs · Trader Passport](https://three.ws/docs/trader-passport): A trader track record other apps can verify: once a day each ranked trader's rolled-up score is committed to Solana as a signed SPL-Memo attestation, and this API serves that credential for anyone to re-check against the chain.
- [Docs · Wallet Portfolio](https://three.ws/docs/portfolio): How the live wallet portfolio works: the keyless Solana-first data sources behind /api/crypto/portfolio, the stable/major/token classification, the honest 24h coverage contract, and the full response shape for agents and scripts.
- [Docs · Airdrop Checker](https://three.ws/docs/airdrops): How the airdrop eligibility checker works: the keyless Solana activity scan and Etherscan V2 EVM scan, the check DSL and scoring thresholds, the honesty contract around unmeasurable and manual criteria, and the full response shape.
- [Docs · Community](https://three.ws/docs/community): Where the three.ws community talks: GitHub Discussions, the Telegram community, the X community, the IBM Community group, and the release channel, with guidance on which room fits which question.
- [Docs · Your first contribution](https://three.ws/docs/first-contribution): Clone to open pull request in about 15 minutes, with a complete worked example: teaching the avatar retargeter a bone-naming convention it did not know, plus the test that proves it.
- [Docs · Triage](https://three.ws/docs/triage): How incoming issues and pull requests get sorted, what every label means, how to claim work, and the response times contributors can expect.
- [Docs · Rigging the pump.fun pill mascot](https://three.ws/docs/pill-mascot): How a static capsule mascot with four nubs became a 52-bone, six-clip avatar: limb discovery from a distance transform, medial-axis skinning, and a bind pose that differs from the rest pose on purpose.
- [Docs · Agent vitals: can it act?](https://three.ws/docs/agent-vitals): Every liveness check was green while ten of twelve autonomous agents had not acted in weeks. Capability attestation models an agent's preconditions as a causal graph and returns the root blocker plus the command that fixes it, instead of a checklist of symptoms.
- [Docs · Terminal renderer](https://three.ws/docs/tty): curl three.ws/tty and a rigged 3D agent walks in your terminal. The hosted streaming endpoint and its parameters, plus @three-ws/tty-3d, the CLI and library that render any GLB in a terminal with a pure-CPU rasterizer: real skeletal animation, half-block pixels, no GPU and no browser.

## Legal

- [Legal](https://three.ws/legal): Every three.ws policy in one place, plus which address to use to report copyright, abuse, or privacy issues.
- [Privacy Policy](https://three.ws/legal/privacy): What data three.ws collects, why we hold it, who we share it with, how long we keep it, and the controls you have over it.
- [End-User License Agreement](https://three.ws/legal/eula): License terms for the three.ws Seeker/Saga mobile app: what the license covers, camera and selfie data, updates, and termination.
- [Terms of Service](https://three.ws/legal/tos): The agreement between you and three.ws: your account, acceptable use, payments and on-chain activity, liability, and DMCA takedowns.
- [Risk Disclosure](https://three.ws/legal/risk): Risk disclosure for real-funds features: experimental software, total-loss risk, autonomous agents, no liability.
- [Content Policy](https://three.ws/legal/content-policy): What you may publish, mint, and monetise on three.ws: prohibited content, agent behaviour, marketplace listings, and how we enforce.
